subject.title: Telegram: per-chat lane serialization (isolated ingress) starves messages.queue.collect — same-chat bursts never coalesce

question: Should Telegram isolated ingress preserve full per-chat handler serialization, or may busy same-lane updates be handed to the existing follow-up/collect queue while the active turn is still running?
rationale: The source path supports the report, but the fix crosses the Telegram spool reliability boundary and the generic reply queue boundary, so maintainers need to choose the intended ordering and retry contract before implementation.

options.title: Bridge Busy Lanes Into Collect
options.body: Route same-lane spooled updates discovered behind an active Telegram handler into the existing follow-up/collect queue with focused crash-window and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Document The Limitation
options.body: Keep per-chat full-handler serialization as the stronger invariant and document that Telegram isolated ingress cannot support same-chat active-turn collect batching today.

options.title: Add A Generic Ingress Queue Seam
options.body: Design a shared channel-ingress handoff API first, then implement Telegram on top of that seam rather than adding a Telegram-only bridge.

recommendation.title: Bridge Busy Lanes Into Collect
recommendation.body: Route same-lane spooled updates discovered behind an active Telegram handler into the existing follow-up/collect queue with focused crash-window and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans both the reply queue ordering work and Telegram boundary refactors.
